# AP-SEC-003 Staff Access, Restricted Items, and Approvals

## 1. Purpose and Scope

This policy establishes procedures for managing staff access to restricted areas within AeroPolicy Airport and the handling of restricted items. It outlines the requirements for requesting access to specific zones and the approval process for carrying restricted items airside. This policy applies to all staff members, including those with access to landside, airside, and baggage make-up areas. It also defines the responsibilities of the Requesting Staff Member, Line Manager, and Security Duty Manager in ensuring compliance with security and safety protocols.

## 2. Staff Access Zones

Staff access to restricted areas is granted based on job responsibilities and security clearance. The landside area is accessible to all staff members who have been authorized for routine operations. Airside access is limited to personnel with a valid airside clearance, which is granted through a formal process. The baggage make-up area is restricted to authorized personnel responsible for baggage handling and security screening. Access to these zones is subject to regular review and may be revoked if an individual fails to comply with security procedures or if their role changes.

## 3. Restricted Items

Restricted items include, but are not limited to, tools, blades, lithium batteries, and flammable liquids. These items pose a risk to safety and security and are subject to strict control measures. Staff members may only carry restricted items into airside areas if they have obtained the necessary approvals. The presence of restricted items in any area of the airport must be reported immediately to the appropriate security personnel. All staff are required to be aware of the types of restricted items and the procedures for handling them.

## 4. Approval Procedure for Restricted Items

Any staff member wishing to carry a restricted item airside must submit a written request to their Line Manager. The request must include a detailed description of the item, its purpose, and the reason for carrying it. The Line Manager is responsible for endorsing the request and ensuring that it aligns with operational requirements. Once endorsed, the request must be forwarded to the Security Duty Manager for final approval. Approval to carry a restricted item airside must be granted in writing by the Security Duty Manager before the item passes the staff screening point. The Security Duty Manager evaluates the request based on safety, security, and operational considerations. All approved requests are recorded and retained for audit purposes.

## 5. Restricted Items Found in Baggage

If a restricted item is found in a checked bag, it is handled in accordance with AP-BAG-001. The item must be removed from the baggage and reported under AP-INC-002. The relevant security personnel are responsible for ensuring that the item is safely secured and that the appropriate authorities are notified. All incidents involving restricted items in baggage must be documented and reviewed to prevent recurrence.

## 6. Records and Review

All requests for restricted items and their approvals are maintained in a secure record. These records are reviewed periodically to ensure compliance with this policy and to identify any areas for improvement. The Security Duty Manager is responsible for overseeing the review process and making recommendations for policy updates. All staff are required to cooperate in the review process and provide any necessary information to support the evaluation.
